title: LinkedIn Help — link post preview image: minimum 1200×627 px, max 5 MB (verified 2026-09-05)
LinkedIn Help — preview frame is a fixed 1.91:1 (1200×627) ratio; off-ratio images are center-cropped
Facebook Sharing docs — use images at least 1200×630; keep as close to 1.91:1 as possible; 600×315 minimum for larger treatment; 8 MB max

X developer forum (official domain) — summary_large_image card is 2:1, historical bounds min 300×157 / max 4096×4096 / <5 MB; X removed its Cards docs from docs.x.com in the 2024–26 migration, so '1200×628' was never an official recommended size
Discord Developer docs — embeds are character-limited only; no pixel dimensions or image size limits documented; embeds scale og:image to fit
Slack docs — classic unfurls read OpenGraph/X-Card metadata; no pixel dimensions, ratios, or size caps documented
Instagram Help — feed photos: width of at least 1080 px; aspect ratio between 1.91:1 and 3:4 (2024 range update)
Instagram Help — Reels ratios/covers (9:16 story/reel de-facto standard)
Bluesky AT Protocol docs — external link cards fetch og:image client-side; no documented thumb dimensions or limits
YouTube Help — custom thumbnails: 4K (3840×2160) now recommended, min width 640 px (videos), JPG/PNG, 2 MB mobile / 50 MB desktop
Pinterest business help — standard pin: 2:3 aspect, 1000×1500 px recommended; taller pins may be cut off in feed

html-to-image README (v1.11.x) — exports toPng/toJpeg/toBlob/toCanvas/toPixelData/toSvg/getFontEmbedCSS; options: width, height, canvasWidth/Height, pixelRatio, quality, backgroundColor, style, filter, cacheBust, preferredFontFormat, fontEmbedCSS, skipAutoScale, type, includeStyleProperties (no skipFonts); fonts inlined by fetching @font-face files and base64-encoding; Safari tested (slower on big DOMs); huge-DOM dataURI limit warning

next/font docs — Google fonts are downloaded and self-hosted as same-origin static assets (empirically proven in-repo by the CapyWrapped export pipeline: document.fonts.ready + html-to-image with no CORS failures)
